introduction.text: The Arch of Malborghetto is an ancient Roman quadrifrons arch located north of Rome on the Via Flaminia, notable for its early fourth‑century construction and its later transformations into a medieval building.

history.description: Construction of the quadrifrons arch in the first half of the fourth century, during the reign of Diocletian.
Transformation into a Greek‑cross church in the eleventh century, closing the archways and adding an apse.
First official notice of the building in 1256, mentioned in a deed of sale by the Orsini family.
Devastation by the Orsini in 1485 to drive out the Colonna family.
Abandonment until the mid‑sixteenth century, when Constantino Pietrasanta rented and rebuilt the structure.
Early twentieth‑century study by Fritz Töbelmann, who confirmed the fourth‑century origin through a brick stamp.

design.description: Original quadrifrons design with rectangular floorplan (14.86 × 11.87 m) and estimated height of 18 m, similar to the Arch of Janus.
Brick masonry visible, with marble plates once attached via metal links; four holes for links still visible.
Giuliano da Sangallo produced the first sketch reconstruction; Fritz Töbelmann also produced sketches; recent 3D models have been created.
